newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki chugs ahead, Nokia and forestries lead.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki chugs ahead, Nokia and forestries lead.

text.p: Finnish shares rose steadily across the board on Monday in moderate trade with U.S. stocks adding to Friday's gains as Wall Street opened, and gains in Nokia and forestries cheered sentiment, brokers said.

Activity in Helsinki and other European bourses was muted with London and Tokyo closed for holidays, bur the German DAX index managed a new record. Total volume in Helsinki was 447 million markka of which Nokia accounted for 34 percent.
The HEX general index rose 0.84 to 2,997.57 points and the FOX derivatives and portfolio benchmark was up 0.92 percent at 1,041.10, just a whisker off its 1,042.81 point session high.
The HEX was rose briefly above the 3,000-point mark and was seen testing it again on Tuesday. "With London open -- I think we might see more gains tomorrow," one broker said.
Nokia ended up 3.00 markka at 331.00, 1.00 markka off its intra-session high.

The forest industry sub-index rose 0.29 percent although UPM-Kymmene fell 0.50 markka to 120.50. Metsa-Serla and Enso advanced strongly, helped by gains in Swedish forestry shares and more favourable prospects for the sector, brokers said.

Finnish options exchange SOP's Pulp Indicator Index put the value of northern bleached softwood pulp at $524.55 per tonne, up from last week's $519.18, boosting hopes that the key price trend indicator for paper products was recovering.
Electronics and furniture subcontractor Incap ended its first day on the OTC list at 51.00 markka, six markka above its 44 markka offering price.

Oil group Neste rose 5.00 markka or almost four percent in fair trade after its petrochemicals group Borealis, co-owned with Norwegian Statoil, posted a sharp rise in its Q1 profits, exceeding expectations, brokers said.
Steel group Rautaruukki was lively, staying well above its recent 42.00 markka offering price as it added 0.20 markka to 47.30 in healthy almost 22 million markka volume.
